title: Reflection of integral finite constant local models across a surjective closed immersion
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and its valuation ring $A=\mathcal O_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a surjective closed immersion of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-surjective-morphism]. On every small pro-étale site $T_{\mathrm{proét}}$ use the pulled-back condensed coefficient ring $B_T=p_T^*\underline A$, with $A$ given its valuation topology [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, def-weil-pbc-small-proetale-site], and module pullback $i^*$ as in [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback]. For a $B_X$-module sheaf $F$, the following are equivalent:

(a) There are a pro-étale covering $\{U_\alpha\to X\}$ and finitely generated $A$-modules $M_\alpha$ such that
$$F|_{U_\alpha}\cong B_{U_\alpha}\otimes_{\underline A}\underline{M_\alpha}.$$
(b) There are a pro-étale covering $\{V_\beta\to Z\}$ and finitely generated $A$-modules $N_\beta$ such that
$$ (i^*F)|_{V_\beta}\cong B_{V_\beta}\otimes_{\underline A}\underline{N_\beta}.$$
The underlined $A$ in $p_T^*\underline A$ denotes the condensed ring associated to the topological ring $A$; underlines in the displayed tensor expressions denote constant sheaves. The displayed tensors are extension of scalars through the constant-section map $\underline A\to B_T$; these are the finite constant local models of [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. The scalar modules may vary with the cover member and may have torsion. No Noetherianity or bounded nilpotence hypothesis on $X$ or $i$ is imposed.

proof.text: The definition HasFiniteConstantLocalModel represents a scalar model by (upperStarFromPoint T).mapMod applied to a finitely presented condensed module P on the point. The canonical monoidal comparison upperStarFromPointComp in [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point-comp] induces Functor.mapModCompIso. Compose its component at P with extension of scalars along condensedPullbackHom. By [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars], extension along this coefficient isomorphism is restriction along its inverse. The unit isomorphism of Mod.comapEquivalenceOfIsIso cancels restriction and extension. Thus f^* C_T(P) is isomorphic to C_S(P), preserving the same P and its finite presentation; flatness and freeness are not needed.

source.place: Extension, clause (2), coequalizer; cartesian-coefficients clause (1) and the module-pullback definition

proof.text: Assume (a). Pull its Scheme.proetalePrecoverage cover back to Z by the standard ZeroHypercover.pullback₁ construction. For each cover member use the pullback square equation and the composition isomorphisms of [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback]. Pull the given local model isomorphism back along the other projection and finish with Step 1. The original finitely presented scalar module is unchanged. The elementary modulePullbackSquare helper expresses this comparison for arbitrary commuting squares before applying it to the chosen pullback projections. The proved exists_pullback_cover interface exposes the pulled-back cover, its index map, its refinement arrows and the square equations existentially; the coefficient functors are then applied to these abstract witnesses, avoiding expensive reduction of chosen scheme pullbacks.

source.place: Tag 09A5, functoriality: base change of the given pro-etale cover

proof.text: Assume (b). Apply [new-lem-weil-pbc-proetale-surjective-closed-cover-refinement] to its cover. This yields a cover B of X and for each b an index a, a cartesian square with maps q:W to B_b and p:W to Z, and r:W to C_a with r followed by C_a to Z equal to p. Closed immersions and surjective morphisms are stable under base change in Mathlib; apply MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderBaseChange.of_isPullback to the flipped square to give both instances on q. No universal-homeomorphism argument is needed.

source.place: Tags 09BK and 09AB: global cover refinement and the cartesian closed fibre

proof.text: For each b, pull the model on C_a back along r. The square equation, the factorization through C_a, and the composition isomorphisms of [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback] identify its left side with q^*(F restricted to B_b). Step 1 identifies its right side with q^* C_B_b(P). By [new-lem-weil-pbc-condensed-surjective-closed-equivalence], this module pullback is an equivalence. Functor.preimageIso lifts the resulting isomorphism by full faithfulness, giving the required local model on B_b with its original finite presentation. This proves (a), without gluing different local models.

tool_uses.why: Generic inverse-image monoidality and colimit preservation compute pullback of the scalar tensor coequalizer; the unit has no separate site-tensor theorem.
Generic global Tag 09BK cover lifting supplies the precise cartesian refinements of a pro-etale covering of Z; no such node occurs in this unit.
Generic geometric base-change stability supplies surjectivity and closedness of the lifted closed fibre, without a nilpotence bound.
Generic equivalence for arbitrary condensed ring modules descends the specified scalar-model isomorphisms; it does not assert the local-model property being proved.
Untwisted coefficient identification ensures pullback uses the same valuation-topological integral ring, on arbitrary schemes.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q148-454e4b7c8 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read in full the item, the four proof steps, every cited statement, the parent det-lem-int-ext-formula steps 3-5 and the unit sk-lem-int-ext. Stacks proetale.tex 09BK (line 4801) and 09AB (line 4963) are checked. I also read the Lean source of condensedSurjectiveClosedPullback_isEquivalence. Its functor is extendScalars(condensedPullbackHom) after mapMod(upperStar Ab), which is exactly the module pullback of sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback, so the coefficient category matches. The statement is true and unchanged: an arbitrary surjective closed immersion, no Noetherian or nilpotence-bound hypothesis, and torsion modules allowed. The parent uses only (b)=>(a), which this item supplies. Step 1 uses colimit preservation, strong monoidality and the coequalizer of sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars(2), so pullback preserves the constant models. Compatibility of alpha_f with the constant-section maps is implicit but routine. Step 2 base-changes the covering and uses the composition isomorphisms. Step 3 uses exactly the IsPullback witnesses of the cover-refinement node; the base change q is a surjective closed immersion, as the equivalence node requires. Step 4 lifts the isomorphism and its inverse by fullness and gets the identities by faithfulness; no gluing is needed. I tested i=id, X empty, Spec k -> Spec k[e]/e^2, and P = 0, O_E, O_E/varpi, O_E/varpi^2. There are no cycles and no SGA. I accept the five declared tool_uses: left-exact inverse-image tensor, cover refinement, universal homeomorphism, condensed equivalence and cartesian coefficients. No new nodes. The closest existing node, lem-sfb-surjective-closed-module-invariance, is for a finite ring with constant sheaves, so it is not a duplicate; the lfp-reflection nodes use sheaf-valued matrices. The Mathlib searches cover all three kinds. No changes.
